title: Lesson Plan — Resources and Development (Class 10 CBSE Geography)
subject: Social Science (Geography)
objectives: Define a resource and classify resources by origin, exhaustibility, ownership and status.
Explain sustainable development and the importance of the 1992 Earth Summit / Agenda 21.
Describe the three steps of resource planning in India.
Identify the main land-use categories and the broad relief composition of India.
Identify causes of land degradation and methods of conservation.
Compare the major soil types of India and their suitability for crops.
prerequisites: Knowledge of physical features of India from earlier classes.
Familiarity with terms like environment, agriculture, mining.
materials: Map of India showing soil types (textbook map)
Cards with soil samples / images of cotton, paddy, cashew nut
A pie-chart of India's relief composition

activities.description: Hook: 'A piece of stone in your school garden — is it a resource?' Discuss conditions (use + technology + culture). Take guesses; introduce the formal definition.
Card-sort: hand out 12 cards (sun, river, oil well, fishery, gold, hydrogen, EEZ tuna, village pond, etc.). Students sort into the four classifications.
Cover four blocks: (i) classification + Agenda 21 / Rio; (ii) resource planning steps; (iii) land use + degradation; (iv) soils + erosion + conservation.
teacher_actions: Drill alluvial / black / red / laterite / arid / forest with regions and crops.
student_actions: Mark soil types on an outline map.
Match soil to crop in pairs.

activities.description: Worksheet practice: 6 questions covering classification, soils, conservation methods, and a short reading on a degraded plot.
Exit ticket: 4 questions, one from each block.
Homework: list 3 resources used at home and classify each on all four classifications.
teacher_actions: Bridge to next chapter (Forest and Wildlife Resources).

homework: Identify the soil type of your district and the dominant crops grown.
List 5 resources used at home and classify each by origin / exhaustibility / ownership / status.
Sketch or describe THREE soil-conservation methods you have seen or read about.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Run a 10-question quiz next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on soil conservation with a 5-point rubric.
references: NCERT Class 10 — Contemporary India – II, Chapter 1: Resources and Development.
